title: Writing a theme for Charlie Barnet
summary: He wrote Barnet's radio theme; Duke let Barnet have extracting done for him.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You were saying about played with Charlie Barnett?

Yeah, Charlie Barnett, I had something that I wrote for myself when I gave it to Charlie, I wrote it for the boys in the band while they were rehearsing, and they used it -- and they used it for quite awhile. The first time when it came on the radio ...
With Charlie Barnett? The opening theme.
Yeah, with Charlie Barnett -- the opening theme.
Did you have a name for it?
Oh, gosh. No, I forgot the thing. (Sings) There was a name for it, but I forgot it. They used a lot of plunges on the trumpet with that tune. But I forgot the name of the thing.
Yeah. Did you do any other writing for Charlie?
No, no. Well, I didn't because he

was the only band that Duke Ellington let somebody else to lend some arrangements, the arranging, because he liked Charlie and Charlie was crazy about Duke Ellington. Charlie thought there was only one band the greatest in the world, and that was Duke Ellington, and he liked his and he asked Duke if he could get some [extracting] work, and we extracted a couple of thing for him.
Uh huh. Do you remember which what tunes?
Didn't you compose things, too, Juan? You said "extracted" all the time.
Charlie, I guess so. Charlie was a good musician.
No, I said YOU extracted and composed, didn't you?
